statement: No medicinal product is sold or supplied until a Qualified Person has certified that each batch was produced and controlled in line with the Marketing Authorisation and other applicable production, control and release regulations.

The manufacturer, and the marketing authorisation holder where different, evaluate the product quality review results and assess whether corrective and preventive action or revalidation is needed under the pharmaceutical quality system.

Audits are carried out at planned intervals to evaluate whether the quality system is effectively implemented and maintained and whether processes and products meet established parameters and specifications.
Records of audit findings are kept and responsibility for follow-up is assigned to prevent recurrence.

No product is sold or supplied until the authorised persons have certified that each batch was produced and controlled in line with the licence and other applicable production, control and release regulations.
The contract describes how rejected starting materials, intermediates, bulk and finished products are handled.

The Site Master File covers general information: a short profile of the firm, the manufacturing activities permitted by the licensing authority, any other activities on the premises, licensed product types with process flow charts, staff numbers in production, QC, storage and distribution, any outside scientific, analytical or technical help, products registered in foreign countries, and short descriptions of the quality management system, pharmaceutical quality system and quality risk assessment.
The Site Master File covers export: the products exported to each country and any related complaints and product recalls.

The Site Master File covers export: the products exported to each country and any related complaints and product recalls.

Medicinal products are not sold or supplied until an Authorised Person has certified that each production batch was made and controlled in line with the Marketing Authorisation and other relevant regulations on production, control and release.

The manufacturer, and the Marketing Authorisation holder where different, evaluate the product quality review results and assess, under the quality system, whether corrective and preventive action or revalidation is needed.

The manufacturing authorisation holder, in its excipient risk assessment, is considering, as a minimum and allowing for the excipient's source, supply chain and use, whether an effective pharmaceutical quality system is established and implemented.

Manufacturers consider keeping regular reports on collecting, treating and disposing of waste and wastewater, at a risk-based frequency consistent with applicable local, regional or international regulatory requirements.
A zero-liquid effluent or zero-discharge approach is adopted, especially where the risk is assessed as high or unclear.
Under the audit SOP, each audit's scope is defined and risk-based criteria pick the most critical activities to audit, including follow-up of CAPAs from the last audit where relevant.

No excipient batch is released and supplied until the quality unit has released it, assured that it was produced and controlled in line with product specifications, this guidance and other relevant regulations on production, control and release.

SOPs and related records are available covering at minimum: equipment; analytical apparatus and instruments; OOS results; maintenance and calibration; cleaning and sanitization; personnel matters such as training, clothing and hygiene; qualification and validation; self-inspection and audits; complaints; recalls; and returns.

The PQS ensures no product is sold or supplied until the authorized persons (see sections 9.11 and 9.12) have certified that each batch was produced and controlled in line with the marketing authorization and any other regulations on production, control and release.
The PQS ensures adequate arrangements exist so that, as far as possible, products are stored, distributed and handled in a way that keeps their quality throughout shelf-life.
The manufacturer, and the marketing authorization holder where different, evaluate the review results and assess, within the PQS, whether CAPA or revalidation is needed.
